kind: Unsigned G09 visual occurrence review proposal

method.sourceReads: Fetched every source CSS listed by navigation from pinned source 3ef84d through GitHub MCP. Recomputed SHA256 of returned UTF-8 bytes and matched every navigation file hash/count.
method.occurrenceIdentity: id = SHA256(JSON.stringify({domain:'source',path,fileSha256,byteOffset,byteLength,seed,encoding:'utf8'})), in that property order, as findOccurrences in the canonical scanner. Files and occurrence rows below reconstruct that exact identity.
method.contextReview: A read-only JavaScript text pass tracked CSS comments, escaped quotes, parentheses, brackets and braces; each seed span was assigned to a complete class token in a qualified-rule prelude or to a comment. All nongenerated selector contexts and all 119 distinct class names were inspected; generated selectors remain stylesheet data behind the palette marker.
method.parserLimit: This was an independent lexical/context review of returned text, not execution of the repository parser, a complete CSS standards parser, an instrumented gate or a browser run. It does not evaluate arbitrary source code.
method.canonicalBoundary: This file is a draft work product, not a canonical review/proof sidecar. All canonicalDisposition fields remain null; no null/empty/fake testObligations are placed into a canonical object.

semanticProposal.appliesOnlyTo: The 1,424 exact source spans recorded below. Archive rows remain candidates pending their own exact contexts. No filename, extension or missing graph entry grants a classification.

selectors.symbolRule: Use the complete class token and its enclosing selector, not just the seed substring.
selectors.producer: The corresponding source stylesheet, or generatePalettes/buildPalette/paletteRules for generated palette CSS.
selectors.consumer: The browser CSS selector matcher. A class selector matches existing DOM classes and supplies visual declarations; it does not read .orchestra configuration directories or derive a repo- profile identifier.
selectors.action: Retain these precise visual identifiers; separately review the code that produces the DOM, chooses a profile, saves permissions or enforces authorization.
selectors.owner: packages/app-shell visual styling; proposed technical ownership, no appointed formal reviewer
selectors.reason: The literal .orchestra is the start of a CSS class identifier. The nine repo- source seeds occur in .actions-repo-strip, .repo-strip, .repo-name and .repo-connection selectors. Neither spelling at these exact CSS positions is a project resolver, store key, request field, filesystem path or permission grant.
limitations: A style selector named profile or permission does not prove the component it styles has migrated identity correctly.
Visibility, disabled appearance and hidden controls do not prove backend denial.
This proposal does not assert every selector has a current matching DOM node; missing graph edges are not proof of inactivity or orphan status.

comment.text: The comment explains that chapter pages carry .orchestra-glass and Home uses the same shared glass styling.
comment.consumer: Developer reading the current CSS comment
comment.reason: The seed names a visual class in an explanatory comment. It is not a config directory or a runtime identity expression. The comment must not be counted as a compiled selector.

observedChain.fact: Both the SF Team web branch and generic AppInterface branch render AppBaseProviders.
CSS @imports include theme, shell, session, review, evidence and brand-identity. Missing JavaScript-graph edges for these styles do not mean they are absent.

The glob imports generated/palette-*.css with ?inline/default. apply uses a catalogued palette id; style writes the resulting CSS to a style element via textContent, not eval. LocalStorage stores a palette choice, not corporate authority.
Finite palette catalog: system/dark/light and five generated recolor palettes.
paletteRules boosts selectors with data-orchestra-palette and emits selected color declarations; generator metadata alone is not a substitute for reading each seed context.

sourceConsumerBindings.limit: The source chain establishes a stylesheet consumer. It is not an observation that every palette was selected or every styled feature exercised in the delivered browser.

testObligation.caseName: the shipped stylesheets are exactly the generator's output

existingExecutedEvidence.logObserved: 1 pass, 0 fail, 15 filtered out, 9 expect calls, in the named case; the workflow first checks the exact test file SHA256.
existingExecutedEvidence.whatItProves: The real selected test reports no generation failures, checks exact generated-directory filenames and compares all seven shipped generated CSS files byte-for-byte to this generator's output.
whatItDoesNotProve: It does not execute the other 15 palette tests or a browser palette-selection journey.
It does not classify all source CSS spans semantically or validate corporate authority.
It does not itself map raw source CSS offsets to minified archive CSS or escaped JavaScript string offsets.
The 41 source occurrences in the files listed below are outside this test's palette input/generated CSS set.
existingExecutedEvidence.note: The existing proof's log hash and authenticated canonical evidence binding must be taken from the preserved real receipt. This draft does not invent them or sign a replacement.

conditions: Read the exact packed bytes and verify each fileSha256 from the current archive inventory; do not derive packed meaning only from a similar source filename.
For each of the 485 CSS occurrences, bind its canonical occurrenceId/byte range to a complete selector class token or explicit comment/value context. Record any other context separately.

For each of the five palette JS modules, parse the complete module without evaluating it and establish whether its relevant literal is static CSS data exported to the palette style consumer. Retain any imports, calls, templates or executable side effects as separate review items.

Decode JavaScript string escapes reproducibly and map each of the 940 raw occurrence spans into the decoded CSS context. A string literal alone is insufficient if its consumer can execute or reinterpret it as authority.

If the build minifies CSS, exact raw source-byte equality is not required by assertion: preserve the actual transformation/structural mapping instead. Never invent equality or source-map endpoints from matching counts.
Join all proposed records to the existing exact occurrence inventory and reject missing/extra IDs. Repeated class names or equal totals do not identify a particular occurrence.
Bind genuine executed obligations and current authenticated review/proofs under the unchanged canonical scanner. No new workflow is requested merely to expand counts.
archiveContextPending.countWarning: The non-generated source subset has 484 occurrences including one comment, while archive CSS has 485. This is a concrete reason not to infer one-to-one packed coverage from counts.

excludedNonPaletteJavaScript.reason: This additional .js path is named for a command-palette component and its inventory reports one worktree seed. Its actual code/context has not been read in this review. It is outside the five identified palette CSS data-module candidates and requires its own exact occurrence and producer/consumer review; no visual classification is assigned.
